strengths: Shop training, scripts, and coworkers as a seen audience match how staff actually talk about phone manner.
Casual friend calls without desu/masu—and therefore without a hinge—is the local split.
Standing up for a business call in some offices is a real leftover habit.

issues.location: How the Body Learns to Follow the Sentence — childhood thanks/apology → phone bow
issues.problem: Children in Japan learn to dip the head with sumimasen. They do not generally bow into a telephone. The section glues school manners to handset training as if they were one classroom.
issues.suggestion: Keep childhood as the source of embodied thanks/apology. Put phone-bowing on retail/office scripts and being visible on the floor. Call the link a later transfer of motor habit, not how kids use phones.

issues.location: “Japanese people rarely narrate this as ‘the spirit of the caller is present.’”
issues.problem: Straw man. Locals would not recognize that inner monologue; they would say ちゃんと応対する.
issues.suggestion: Quote the local register: looking proper, not sounding bored, matching the customer—already in the next sentences. Cut the spirit line.
